title: Use-case boundaries and practical modular design
outcome: Separate transport, business rules, persistence, and external adapters without creating needless layers.
useCase: Features called from controllers, imports, and jobs.
benefits: Rules remain reusable and easier to test.
drawbacks: Unnecessary abstractions can obscure a simple feature.
cue: Name the action. Protect the rule. Isolate real boundaries.

trace.title: Transport input
trace.detail: A use case names an action, such as AssignTicket. It receives validated intent and a trusted actor, checks the rule, coordinates persistence, and returns a result. A controller translates HTTP into that action. A scheduled job can call the same use case through a different entry point.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Trace the same assignment from HTTP and a background import. Both must enforce the core transition rule. Then replace only the remote receipt adapter with a fake and test the use-case result.

For a new requirement, identify which boundary changes. A new HTTP representation need not rewrite the domain rule. A new provider should mostly change an adapter if its semantics fit the existing contract.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A service layer that merely forwards every call without a decision may add noise. Distributed services do not remove shared data/contract problems; they move them across a network.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Separate transport, business rules, persistence, and external adapters without creating needless layers. Explain one example and one failure.
